explanation:

              distinguishes them from soft ferromagnetic or other materials.

question_text: Why do magnetic field lines never intersect, unlike some electric field lines in complex charge distributions?

options.text:
(3)
The field direction would be ambiguous at the intersection

explanation:
Magnetic field lines represent the direction of the magnetic field at each point. If they intersected, it
              would imply two different directions for the field at the same point, which is physically impossible. This
              uniqueness stems from the vector nature of the magnetic field and the absence of magnetic monopoles.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Magnetism and Matter / Test 1

              external field is removed. Their domains, which align strongly in the presence of a field, return to a
              random orientation due to minimal internal resistance, unlike hard ferromagnets.

question_text: The reason a magnetic field does not exert a force along its own direction on a moving charge is:

options.text:
(1)
The force is perpendicular to the field

(2)
The field cancels the charge’s motion

(3)
The force aligns with the field lines

(4)
The charge moves parallel to the field

explanation:
The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by F=q(v×B), which is
              always perpendicular to both the velocity v and the magnetic field B. Thus,
              the force has no component along the field direction, as the cross product ensures orthogonality.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Magnetism and Matter / Test 3

question_text: The reason a superconductor can levitate a magnet is:
explanation:
Superconductors exhibit perfect diamagnetism (Meissner effect), expelling all magnetic field lines from
              their interior by inducing surface currents that create an opposing field. This repulsion allows them to
              levitate a magnet, a phenomenon unique to their zero permeability state.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Magnetism and Matter / Test 3

question_text: If a bar magnet is broken into two pieces, each piece retains both a north and a south pole. This observation supports the idea that:

options.text:
(2)
Magnetic fields can be shielded completely

(4)
The magnet loses its magnetism upon breaking

explanation:
Unlike electric charges, magnetic poles cannot be isolated. Breaking a magnet creates two smaller
              magnets, each with its own north and south pole, indicating that magnetic monopoles do not exist in
              nature, a key principle in magnetism.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Magnetism and Matter / Test 8

question_text: A material placed in a magnetic field increases the field inside it slightly and moves toward stronger field regions. This behavior is characteristic of:
explanation:
Paramagnetic materials have a small positive susceptibility (χ>0), causing a slight
              enhancement of the magnetic field inside them due to the weak alignment of atomic magnetic moments with
              the external field. They are attracted to regions of stronger field strength.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Magnetism and Matter / Test 8

question_text: Which property of magnetic field lines distinguishes them from electric field lines in the context of a dipole?

options.text:
(2)
They originate and terminate on charges

(3)
They intersect at points of high field strength

explanation:
Magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops because there are no magnetic monopoles; they emerge
              from the north pole and enter the south pole, looping back internally. In contrast, electric field lines
              of a dipole start at the positive charge and end at the negative charge, or extend to infinity if
              unterminated.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Magnetism and Matter / Test 8

question_text: A magnetic dipole in a uniform field is in unstable equilibrium when:

options.text:
(1)
It is perpendicular to the field

(2)
It is parallel to the field

(3)
It is anti-parallel to the field

explanation:
The potential energy U=−mBcos⁡θ is maximized when θ=180∘
              (anti-parallel), making it an unstable equilibrium position. Any small perturbation causes the dipole to
              rotate toward the stable position (θ=0∘), as the energy decreases in that direction.

The field exerts a constant force

The dipole’s poles repel each other

options.text:
(1)
A net force toward the field source

explanation:

question_text: When a magnetic dipole is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, the torque acting on it is maximum because:

options.text:
(1)
The angle between the dipole moment and field is 90°

(2)
The dipole moment cancels the field

(4)
The dipole aligns with the field lines

explanation:
The torque on a magnetic dipole is given by τ=mBsin⁡θ. It reaches its maximum value
              when sin⁡θ=1, which occurs at θ=90∘ (perpendicular orientation), as the
              cross product m×B is greatest when the angle between the dipole moment and field is 90
              degrees.
